ideas.name: sarrus_straight_jaw
ideas.description: An exact straight-line moving jaw built from revolute joints only (a Sarrus linkage). A base plate is screwed where the stock moving jaw's hinge was, and a finger plate carries the stock-length finger (81 mm drop) with the printed pads. Two chains of two 55 mm PLA links join the plates. Chain A's hinges lie along the depth axis, so its elbow folds upward toward the wrist; the servo horn drives its base hinge. Chain B's hinges are vertical, so its elbow folds sideways along the object's depth, at wrist height. The two non-parallel chains force the finger plate to translate along the closing axis with no rotation and no rise. Opening = 2L cos(phi): about 10-106 mm with phi from 85 to 15 deg (keep phi above 12 deg, away from the straight-out singularity). Squeeze = 1.62 N*m / (2L sin phi): 15 N narrow, about 30 N at 96 mm. Pad_angle should be retuned to about 0-15 deg on this jaw.

proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face / squeezed_down_out / fixed_jaw_missed: all five failing objects are 73-96 mm wide and only 30-58 mm tall. At those openings the revolute jaw's fingertip rises above the fixed one (+14 mm at 75 mm, +23 mm at 85 mm, +35 mm at 95 mm), and its face tilts 44-64 deg. On the low boxes the moving finger lands on the top face: the pudding box takes 28 N pushing 85 deg down at +17 mm, against a top at +19. On the gelatin box the contact is tilted 45-50 deg, so N sin(a) pushes the box down and out of the grip.
proposals.principle: A finger that slides straight along the closing axis neither turns nor rises, so at every opening its contact stays horizontal, opposed to the fixed face and low on the object's side. Squeeze is servo torque divided by the sector radius.
proposals.hypothesis: No value of the current parts fixes this. The revolute jaw's rise and tilt are fixed by its geometry. Pads at 45 deg still leave +14 deg and +14 mm at 85 mm. The parallelogram at link 90 rises +33 mm at 85 mm. The prismatic pinion and the slide at radius 30 only open to 68 mm, too narrow for objects 73-96 mm wide. long_slide at sector_radius_mm=50 opens to 103 mm, and at 35, 55 and 85 mm it gives a face at 0 deg, a tip at +1 mm and 32 N. That covers the mustard bottle (96 mm, about 3.5 mm of clearance per side) and everything narrower. Grip check: sugar 2*0.5*32 = 32 N against 5.0 N of weight; mustard 2*0.4*32 = 25.6 N against 4.2 N; the cans 2*0.35*32 = 22 N against 3.4 N. The arm carries it: 0.41 + 0.15*5.14 = 1.18 N*m, under the 1.62 N*m stall, so the 12 V servos ($68, refused) are not needed. Cost: $6.40 to buy (2 lm3uu bearings, 2 steel_rod_3x150), m3 screws on hand, 43 g PLA = 216 machine min, 3 days lead.
risks: Round objects (apple, golf_ball, tennis_ball, racquetball, plum, lemon, strawberry, tomato_soup_can): these are now held between parallel flat faces instead of a slightly tilted one. Because the tip stays at +1 mm, System 1 can set the contact at the equator, where the contacts are antipodal and horizontal. 32 N is more squeeze than the current 20 N.

Small objects (dice 17 mm, large_marker 19 mm): the travel is about 96 mm (50 mm/rad over 1.92 rad), so the jaw still closes to about 7 mm, below 17 mm. The extra squeeze on the light objects is harmless.
Wrist mass goes up by the steel rods and 43 g of print. The arm torque margin above stays well under stall.

proposals.edit: jaw -> long_slide (sector_radius_mm=48)
proposals.mechanism: Two related failures on objects 73-96 mm wide: either the moving jaw lands on the top face, or it squeezes the object down and out. Both come from the hinged jaw rising and tilting at wide openings: the fingertip is +14 mm and the face 44 deg off at 75 mm, +23 mm and 53 deg at 85 mm, +35 mm and 64 deg at 95 mm. On these 30-58 mm tall objects the tip rides over the top and presses down at 45-87 deg; on the tuna can and one sugar box run neither jaw touched the object at all.
proposals.principle: Two contacts hold an object when their normals are horizontal and opposed. A finger that slides straight neither turns nor rises, so it stays parallel at every opening and reaches below a low object's top. The slide's travel is the sector radius in mm per servo radian, so the radius sets the widest opening.
proposals.hypothesis: No value of the current parts fixes the hinge's rise (see the brief: pads at 45 deg still leave +14 deg and +14 mm at 85 mm). The 60-tooth pinion slide stops at 68 mm, and the four-bar rises 33 mm. The long slide at radius 50 opens to 103 mm with the tip at +1 mm, but it was refused for a 1.6 x 0.2 x 0.5 mm overlap with the wrist at the extreme of the roll. Taking 2 mm off the sector radius should clear that overlap while still opening to about 68 + (48-30) x 35/20 = 99.5 mm, enough for the 96 mm mustard bottle. Squeeze is about 33 N. The sugar box then gets 2 x 0.5 x 33 = 33 N of grip against 5.0 N of weight, and the shoulder needs 0.41 + 0.15 x 5.14 = 1.18 N*m, under the 1.62 N*m stall. Cost: $6.40 (2 x lm3uu_bearing at $1.20, 2 x steel_rod_3x150 at $2), 3 days lead, about 216 machine minutes, within $40, 7 days and 600 minutes.
risks: Rolling round objects (golf_ball, apple, tennis_ball, racquetball, lemon, plum, strawberry, tomato_soup_can): a flat parallel pair doesn't centre a sphere. The fingertips stay level, though, so System 1 can put the contacts at the equator where the push is purely horizontal, and these objects are light (at most 68 g; the 349 g soup can lies with its axis along the jaws).
flat_screwdriver and the 370 g potted_meat_can: the squeeze is about 33 N against a force limit that tripped near 56 N before, and System 1's close target sets how hard the jaw presses.
dice (17 mm): at radius 48 the slide closes to about 7-10 mm, so the small objects are still in reach.
The slide could still overlap the wrist if the overlap scales with more than the radius; in that case it is refused before any trial and nothing held is lost.

I'm sending three proposals: two free pad tweaks aimed at the tuna fish can, and one new jaw idea for the other three failing objects. Neither tweak is likely to fix those three.

**Why the four objects fail.** All are wide (85–96 mm). On the hinged jaw, the moving fingertip rises as it opens: +24 mm above the fixed one at 85 mm, with its face 30° off parallel. So it lands on the object's top instead of its side.
- **Mustard bottle (96 mm):** out of reach with any pad setting. The jaw opens to 93 mm at most, 95 mm with the pads tilted 45°.
- **Pudding box (90 mm) and sugar box (92 mm):** even at the 45° tilt, the tip still rises about 17 mm or more at those widths.

**Proposals 1 and 2: re-tilt the pads ($0, all parts on hand).** Tilting the pads 40° already gained the tuna can and the gelatin box (iteration 1). Its only loss was the banana, which hit the force limit at 0.02 s. That is a collision as the hand is placed, not a grip that slipped.
- **Proposal 1:** tilt 40°, pads narrowed from 12 to 8 mm and the rubber skin thinned from 2 to 1 mm, aimed at that collision. Narrowing hasn't been tried.
- **Proposal 2:** tilt 38° at full 12 mm width with the thinner skin. It's a fallback in case narrow pads lose grip on long objects. It may be too little tilt to gain the tuna can.

Both change the pads, so they will be tried separately, not together.

**Proposal 3: a new jaw part (recorded, not tested).** The catalogue's sliding jaw (sector radius 41–46 mm) did gain the pudding box, sugar box and tuna can. But on every setting tried, its gear rack pressed down on the tops of the banana, both cans and the apple. Its 50 mm radius is refused because it collides with the wrist.

My idea is a slide with the rack mounted on the outer side, clear of the gap between the fingers, and a finger hanging about 60 mm below the rails. Its gear sector (radius 52 mm) has a 3 mm cut-out on the arc that faces the wrist, so it passes the no-collision rule, and it opens to about 98 mm.

It would need to be bought and printed: 2 linear bushings and 2 steel rods for $6.40, with 3 days' lead time, plus about 283 machine minutes. That fits the $40, 7 days and 594 minutes left. The 12 V servo upgrade is still out at $68 and isn't needed: holding the 514 g sugar box with this jaw needs about 1.26 N·m at the shoulder, under the 1.62 N·m the current servos give.

idea.name: sarrus_straight_jaw
idea.description: An exact straight-line moving jaw built from revolute joints only (a Sarrus linkage). A base plate is screwed where the stock moving jaw's hinge was, and a finger plate carries the stock-length finger (81 mm drop) with the printed pads. Two chains of two 55 mm PLA links join the plates. Chain A's hinges lie along the depth axis, so its elbow folds upward toward the wrist; the servo horn drives its base hinge. Chain B's hinges are vertical, so its elbow folds sideways along the object's depth, at wrist height. The two non-parallel chains force the finger plate to translate along the closing axis with no rotation and no rise. Opening = 2L cos(phi): about 10-106 mm with phi from 85 to 15 deg (keep phi above 12 deg, away from the straight-out singularity). Squeeze = 1.62 N*m / (2L sin phi): 15 N narrow, about 30 N at 96 mm. Pad_angle should be retuned to about 0-15 deg on this jaw.
idea.test: A jaw builder that models a translating moving finger driven through the nonlinear transmission d = 2L cos(phi) (ratio 2L sin phi mm per rad). Its collision geometry should be only the finger plus links and base plate at stock hinge height (81 mm above the fingertip), with elbows folding up and sideways. Parameter link_mm in [45, 60]. Re-run all 21 groups with pads pad_angle 0-15 and groove 0-2.

idea.name: flexure_self_aligning_moving_pad
idea.description: A moving-jaw pad whose face plate (PLA, 0.5 mm TPU skin) hangs on a TPU living hinge along its bottom edge. A light preload from the hinge holds it against a printed hard stop at the current 30 deg tilt. Contacts below the hinge, or pushing the face toward its stop (any opening where the face is swung bottom-in, i.e. every held object up to about 50 mm), just push the plate against the stop. The pad then behaves exactly like today's 30 deg pad, so the held groups see the same body. When the face is swung bottom-out (wide openings), the box's top edge touches the plate above the hinge first. That turns the plate outward about its bottom edge, by up to +40 deg, until it lies flat on the box's vertical side. The contact becomes a face with a horizontal normal, square against the fixed jaw. The fixed pad is unchanged. A moving pad 3 mm thick instead of 4 gives about 1 mm more opening (about 96 mm), which could bring the mustard bottle within reach.

I'm proposing the long slide again, at two new settings. I don't expect any pad setting on the current hinged jaw to fix these failures, and I can't promise either proposal keeps every held object.

**The failure.** All four objects fail the same way: the moving fingertip ends up on the top face (moving_jaw_on_top_face). At 75-85 mm apart, the hinged jaw's moving fingertip sits +13 to +22 mm above the fixed one, and its face leans +19 to +28 deg. That edge lands on the tops of these 34-45 mm tall objects and pushes down at 71-89 deg.

**Why not cheaper moves.**
- **Pad settings:** 8 trials, 0 gains. Tilting the pad 33 deg or more loses the banana, and even the 45 deg maximum still leaves the face +14 deg off parallel at 85 mm.
- **12 V servos:** refused, since they cost $68 and $40 is left. They also add lifting torque, which doesn't change where the fingertip lands.
- **Parallelogram jaw:** its fingertip rises +44 mm at 85 mm.
- **Prismatic jaw:** opens only 62 mm, too narrow for these objects.

**Why the long slide.** It is the only catalogue part whose fingertip stays level (+2 mm at every opening), and in earlier trials it gained the pudding box, sugar box and tuna can. Every time it was rejected, the cause was the tall objects (apple, potted meat can, tomato soup can): the rack or pad hit their tops because the finger doesn't reach far enough below the rack. Seven slide trials only tried pad extensions of 12 mm (lost the 3 tall objects) and 28 mm (lost 7 objects). Nothing in between was ever tested, so I'm proposing 20 mm and 24 mm to find a value that clears the tall objects without the 28 mm losses. A 15 deg pad tilt lost no more objects than 30 deg did. The 0.5 mm TPU skin keeps friction at 0.9.

**Cost:** each proposal is $6.40 (2 LM3UU bushings at $1.20 and 2 steel rods of 3x150 mm at $2), 3 days lead time and about 216 machine minutes. That fits the $40, 7 days and 591 minutes left.

**Not expected to pass:** the mustard bottle, which at 96 mm is at the 97 mm limit of the widest slide.

**Contingency:** if both fail on the tall objects again, the next step is an outboard-rack design that drops the finger lower, recorded earlier as an untested idea (outboard_rack_drop_finger_slide), rather than more slide parameter trials.

idea.name: graded_counter_rotation_fourbar_pad
idea.description: The moving pad pivots on an MR63 bearing pin at the stock moving fingertip. A 15 mm crank on the pad's upper end connects through a printed tie rod (about 81 mm, two MR63 bearings) to a ground pin on a printed clamp boss on the gripper body, offset about 15 mm from the jaw hinge. This makes a four-bar whose coupler is the pad. With the tie rod exactly as long as the 81 mm hinge-to-pin arm, the pad keeps a fixed world angle. Making it 2-3 mm off parallel grades the angle: about -20 deg (bottom in) at 17-35 mm, as today's 30 deg pad, passing through vertical at about 85-92 mm and staying within about +5 deg at 95 mm. The tip path, the 95 mm opening and the 20 N squeeze are unchanged because the servo still swings the stock jaw. The tie rod runs outboard of the 12 mm pad width, so nothing extends into the object's space or below the fingertip. The pad keeps the 0.5 mm TPU skin (friction 0.9) and the fixed jaw is untouched.
idea.test: Builder: model the moving pad as its own body on a hinge joint at the moving fingertip, plus a tie-rod body hinged to the gripper frame and to the pad crank (closed with an equality/connect constraint). Parameters: tie-rod length offset (-4 to +4 mm from parallel), crank length (10-20 mm) and ground pivot offset. Sweep openings 17-95 mm to report face angle and tip height, as the brief does. Then run all 21 groups, checking that the face is within ±5 deg of vertical at 85-92 mm and matches today's 18-23 deg bottom-in at 17-35 mm.

proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face. On the hinge, the moving fingertip rises and the face swings out at wide openings: +22 mm and 28 deg at 85 mm, +34 mm and 38 deg at 95 mm. At 90 to 96 mm the pad lands on the top of a 34 to 58 mm tall object, pushing 70 to 89 deg down, and the fixed jaw never touches. Earlier long_slide trials lost potted_meat_can and tomato_soup_can (and apple) to a second problem: the slide's pad kept a 15 to 30 deg tilt. The pad's bottom edge landed on the can tops (14 N on top at +42, top at +42), or the pad intersected the object at placement (force_limit at t=0.02 s).
proposals.principle: Hold with antipodal contacts: horizontal normals facing each other. A slide's finger neither turns nor rises (brief: tip +2 mm at every width), so its face is parallel at every opening only when the pad itself is not tilted. pad_angle exists to cancel the hinge's rotation. On a slide it has nothing to cancel, so it tilts the face by the full angle for good (brief: face -30 deg at every width). That 30 deg tilt (tan 30 = 0.58) is more than the 0.35 friction of the metal cans. A longer reach raises the rack higher above the contact for the tall objects.
proposals.hypothesis: Every earlier slide trial kept pad_angle at 15 or 30 to protect the rollers, and the one angle-0 trial also used a 28 mm reach that could explain its losses. That leaves two things to test on the slide: a level pad with a moderate reach, and a groove to centre the rollers. At r=46 the slide already gained pudding, sugar, tuna and gelatin. With a vertical pad face (pad_angle 0) the inward-leaning pad bottom that landed on the can tops and hit objects at t=0.02 s is gone. Pudding box (90 mm), sugar box (92 mm) and mustard bottle (96 mm) cannot be fixed with any part the catalogue allows within budget:

- **Parallelogram:** its tip rises 44 mm at 85 mm.
- **Prismatic:** it opens only to 62 mm.
- **12 V servos:** refused on budget ($68 needed, $40 left), and they do not touch this geometric failure.
